title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named campus destinations for studying, meeting, recharging, exercising, and joining hands-on community activities between classes.

cards.title: Match the Seat to the Assignment
cards.subtitle: Group tables, individual cubicles, booths, and computer access
cards.notes: Choose a booth or group table for collaboration, an individual cubicle for focused work, or a library computer when you need campus equipment.
cards.short_summary: Greenley offers distinct seating modes for solo work, group study, and online classes.
cards.evidence_claim: The current library FAQ says Greenley Library provides group tables and booths, individual cubicles, comfortable chairs, computers, laptops, Wi-Fi, and group seating.
cards.access_notes: The library is open seven days when classes are in session; consult its current homepage for daily and special hours. Group spaces are not reserved in advance.

cards.title: Use the Lounges Between Business Classes
cards.subtitle: Lounge areas and vending machines on all three floors
cards.notes: Head to the lounge area on the floor nearest your next class, then use the vending machines without crossing campus during a short break.
cards.short_summary: Three floors of lounge space make the School of Business useful for brief study gaps.
cards.evidence_claim: Farmingdale State College's current Academic Advisement Handbook lists lounge areas with vending machines on all three floors of the School of Business as places to study and meet.
cards.access_notes: Use during normal building access and yield lounge seating when academic or college activities require the space.

cards.title: Take the Meeting Outside at Bunche Plaza
cards.subtitle: Benches, a fountain, international flags, and campus events
cards.notes: Use the benches for an outdoor conversation or reading break, and check the event calendar before assuming the plaza will be quiet.
cards.short_summary: The flag-lined plaza combines outdoor seating with a documented campus gathering role.
cards.evidence_claim: The college identifies Bunche Plaza's benches as a place to study and meet; its visitor page documents the fountain, international flags, Fountain Fest, and Earth Day celebrations there.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access is weather-dependent, and scheduled college events may temporarily change how the plaza is used.

cards.title: Find a Campus Center Base Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Two open lounges, cafeterias, meeting rooms, and outdoor seating
cards.notes: Start with an open lounge for casual work; move to the outdoor tables when weather permits, and leave dining seats available during busy meal periods.
cards.short_summary: The Campus Center supports informal work indoors and outside as well as dining and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2025–2026 college catalog says the Campus Center has a student lounge and two small meeting rooms; the current advising handbook lists two open lounges and outdoor tables and benches.
cards.access_notes: The 2025–2026 catalog lists Monday–Friday hours of 7:00 a.m.–midnight and weekend hours of 10:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m.; verify schedule changes before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Quintyne Hall Meditation and Prayer Space
cards.title: Reset Quietly in Quintyne Hall
cards.subtitle: A campus-listed meditation and prayer destination
cards.notes: Use this designated space for a quiet personal pause, keep devices silent, and respect others' reflective or religious practices while sharing it.
cards.short_summary: Quintyne Hall provides a specifically identified setting for meditation or prayer.
cards.evidence_claim: The current Farmingdale State College Academic Advisement Handbook lists Quintyne Hall's Meditation (Prayer) space among campus places to study and meet.
cards.access_notes: Use during permitted building access and observe any posted room rules, closures, or scheduled uses.

cards.title: Settle Into a Gleeson Lounge
cards.subtitle: Second- and third-floor lounges plus lobby counter seating
cards.notes: Try the lobby counter for a short laptop task or move upstairs for lounge seating when you have a longer gap between health-sciences classes.
cards.short_summary: Gleeson supplies several informal seating choices across its lobby and upper floors.
cards.evidence_claim: The current Academic Advisement Handbook identifies lounges on Gleeson Hall's second and third floors plus bar stools and a counter in the front lobby.
cards.access_notes: Use during normal academic-building access and follow posted restrictions for nearby classrooms, laboratories, and departmental areas.

cards.title: Pair a Hale Hall Break With the Gallery
cards.subtitle: First- and second-floor lounges near Memorial Gallery
cards.notes: Use either floor's lounge for a between-class pause, then check Memorial Gallery's current exhibition page before adding a gallery visit.
cards.short_summary: Hale combines two documented lounge areas with an active campus exhibition space.
cards.evidence_claim: The advising handbook lists lounge areas on Hale Hall's first and second floors, while the Memorial Gallery page confirms that the college gallery is located in Hale Hall.
cards.access_notes: Gallery admission is free, but the college asks visitors to call ahead. Lounge access follows Hale Hall's operating conditions and scheduled activities.

cards.title: Choose an Indoor or Outdoor Lupton Stop
cards.subtitle: Two floors of lounges plus benches at both building entrances
cards.notes: Use an indoor lounge when you need a work surface, or take a short outdoor break on the front or rear benches when conditions are comfortable.
cards.short_summary: Lupton offers both indoor lounge areas and outdoor seating on two sides of the building.
cards.evidence_claim: The current advising handbook lists first- and second-floor lounge areas in Lupton Hall and outdoor benches at both the front and rear of the building.
cards.access_notes: Indoor access follows academic-building operations; outdoor benches are subject to weather, construction, and campus events.

cards.title: Build Movement Into a Campus Gap
cards.subtitle: Gym, exercise room, lockers, showers, and recreation facilities
cards.notes: Bring your Farmingdale ID, check current recreation access, and choose equipment or open activity space that fits the time before your next commitment.
cards.short_summary: Nold gives students a named campus destination for exercise and recreation between obligations.
cards.evidence_claim: The current advising handbook lists Nold Hall's equipped gym, exercise room, lockers, and showers; Campus Recreation documents fitness, group exercise, and intramural programs.
cards.access_notes: Access may require a valid Farmingdale ID and depends on current recreation schedules, team use, classes, and event closures.

cards.title: Join a Scheduled Giving Garden Work Session
cards.subtitle: Twelve growing beds supporting the FSC Food Pantry
cards.notes: Email the Sustainability Manager to arrange a volunteer shift, then follow the garden's maintenance plan instead of tending or harvesting independently.
cards.short_summary: The garden turns scheduled student and community work into produce for the campus pantry.
cards.evidence_claim: FSC says the Giving Garden has 12 beds, donates most of its produce to the FSC Food Pantry, and offers scheduled or regular volunteer opportunities.
cards.access_notes: Volunteer participation must be arranged with the campus Sustainability Manager; consult the campus map's sustainability layer for the garden location.
